description: REQ-508's EARS clause -- the requirement's own most-authoritative sentence -- makes a false claim about the shipped code's structure, introduced BY the very citation-audit fix (converge iter3 -> iter4 mechanical sweep, FIND-007's rewrite) that was supposed to have made every citation in this document mechanically re-verified and exhaustively accurate. behavioral-spec.md:509-510 reads: 'the escalation call sites this requirement's own EARS clause describes are `index.mjs:878`/`:914` inside `writeAlwaysActEscalation`'. This is only half true: `index.mjs:914` IS inside `writeAlwaysActEscalation` (function spans index.mjs:899-920, confirmed by grep and direct read), but `index.mjs:878` is NOT -- it is inside a completely different function, `writeWakeErrorAndSleep` (spans index.mjs:868-883, confirmed by grep: `grep -n '^async function writeWakeErrorAndSleep|^async function writeAlwaysActEscalation' runtime/loop/index.mjs` returns `868:async function writeWakeErrorAndSleep(...)` and `899:async function writeAlwaysActEscalation(...)`). `writeWakeErrorAndSleep` is the shared THINK-transport-failure handler (its own JSDoc at index.mjs:862-867 says so explicitly) -- a structurally distinct code path from REQ-508's exhausted-retry-bound escalation, which is what `writeAlwaysActEscalation` (index.mjs:899-920) actually implements. The number 878 is not stale (a `appendHarnessFailure` call genuinely exists at that exact line) -- the citation-audit's grep-based method (confirm the substring/construct exists at the cited line) correctly verified the LINE NUMBER but never checked the ENCLOSING-FUNCTION claim wrapped around it, so this over-claim survived the 'mechanical, exhaustive, 0 DRIFTED remaining' sweep. The identical over-claim is also baked into the citation-audit's own evidence artifact (evidence/citation-audit-2026-07-11.md row 27's 'Description' column: 'Escalation call sites: `index.mjs:878`/`:914` (`writeAlwaysActEscalation`)') and into behavioral-spec.md's iter3 Changelog entry's parenthetical ('call sites `613`/`767`/`878`/`914`' -- this specific listing does not itself claim same-function, so it is technically accurate as a flat list, but it is presented immediately alongside the EARS-clause claim that IS wrong). verification-architecture.md and verification-report.md do NOT repeat this specific over-claim (verification-report.md:121 correctly cites `index.mjs:899-910` for `writeAlwaysActEscalation` with no mention of 878), so this is a single-location, non-propagated defect -- unlike FIND-005/006/007's multi-site drift -- but it sits inside the one sentence REQ-508 itself designates as its EARS clause, the same category FIND-003 already treated as blocking when found stale for REQ-513 (behavioral-spec.md's own converge-iter2 Changelog entry: 'REQ-513's own EARS clause (most authoritative sentence)'). Zero behavioral/test impact: `writeWakeErrorAndSleep`'s own appendHarnessFailure call (878) and `writeAlwaysActEscalation`'s own appendHarnessFailure call (914) both function correctly and are both exercised by the passing 183/183 suite; only the spec's structural description of WHERE 878 lives is wrong.
